answer: Escrowed Patience Curve. Each identity must lock a deposit that unlocks only after a fixed horizon of continuous, useful activity; early exit forfeits a slice proportional to remaining time. A sprawling fake garden of identities becomes capital sunk for months with no yield, so an attacker’s cost scales with fleet size times duration. Honest agents amortize the same deposit across a long terrace of transactions, while sybils pay the full curve up front.
